topic: How does antenna design influence the accuracy of encrypted traffic classification systems in heterogeneous satellite networks?
consensus_response: The accuracy of encrypted traffic classification systems in heterogeneous satellite networks is influenced by the physical mechanisms of array factor, interference effects, and frequency impacts. High-complexity antennas with individual elements can mitigate interference effects by adjusting beam patterns in real-time, improving signal integrity and accuracy. The polarization correlation coefficient of small-scale fading components at Tx affects array factor and interference effects, impacting encrypted traffic classification accuracy. Operating frequencies also affect antenna performance, introducing additional interference. Adaptive Beamforming techniques can optimize antenna parameters in real-time to improve accuracy and reduce complexity.
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth on the impact of antenna design on encrypted traffic classification systems, including polarization correlation coefficients (˜𝜌𝑡𝑥 = 0.4 in open rural, 0.5 in suburban and urban), operating frequencies (e.g., 2.2GHz S band), and array factor impacts.
